reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Designation of the state registrar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and section history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Designates the department director or the director's designee as state registrar of vital statistics.

headings.title: Vital statistics administration, training, forms, reports, and data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note. Covers system administration, uniformity training programs, prescribing/furnishing forms or alternative data-transmission means under sections 193.005 to 193.325, publishing vital statistics and rule-required reports, and transmitting department-owned copies or data to state or local health agencies under registrar-governed uses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.045:9904 (2 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(4) of subsection 2) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, numbering, and all bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked registrar designation, 193.005–193.325 cross-references, and department property/use controls over health-agency data. Retained both drafted titles as accurate and concise.

headings.title: Minimum federal items on certificate and report forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2021 H.B. 429 merged with H.B. 432). Requires certificate and report forms under sections 193.005 to 193.325 or regulations to include at minimum the items recommended by the federal national vital statistics agency. Independent review refined title from "forms and reports" to "certificate and report forms" to match the statutory phrase "forms of certificates and reports".

headings.title: Forms and formats prescribed by state registrar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires every certificate, report, and other document under sections 193.005 to 193.325 to use a form or format prescribed by the state registrar.

headings.title: Date received for registration on vital records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires all vital records to contain the date received for registration.

headings.title: Photographic, electronic, or other filing and registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Expresses permissive ('may') authority to file and register required information by photographic, electronic, or other state-registrar-prescribed means.

headings.title: Parents' Social Security numbers, agency access, and limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers parents furnishing Social Security numbers for birth certificates subject to federal HHS good-cause exceptions, exclusion from the birth certificate itself, sharing with the Family Support Division (child-support purpose limit and section 454.440 confidentiality/penalties) and Children's Division (parent-identity verification and section 210.156 confidentiality), and preservation of DHSS statistical use.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.075:49780 (5 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2021 merged H.B. 429 & H.B. 432), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive ("may") filing in (4) and SSN good-cause exception, birth-certificate exclusion, FSD/Children's Division purpose limits (454.440, 210.156), and DHSS statistical use in (5). Revised subsection 1 title to "Minimum federal items on certificate and report forms"; retained subsections 2–5.

headings.title: Filing and registering live birth certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 1997 S.B. 361, A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49). Covers five-day filing of live birth certificates with the local registrar or as directed by the state registrar, and registration conditioned on completion and filing under this section.

headings.title: Births in or en route to institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers duties of the person in charge of an institution (or representative) to prepare, certify via signature or approved electronic process, and file within five days, the attending physician or attendant's five-day medical certification, and institutional fallback completion if not timely certified.

headings.title: Filing priority for births outside institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Sets the ordered priority of persons required to prepare and file certificates for non-institutional births: attending physician, other attendant, or father, mother, or person in charge of the premises.

headings.title: Births on moving conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguishes U.S. moving-conveyance births first removed in Missouri (removal place treated as birthplace) from international waters, air space, or foreign-country conveyance births first removed in Missouri (actual birthplace shown insofar as determinable).

headings.title: Husband as father and marital paternity exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Covers entering the husband as father when the mother was married at conception, birth, or in between, subject to court paternity determinations or three-party affidavits under section 193.215 establishing a legal finding of paternity.

headings.title: Court orders determining paternity and surname
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires entering the father's name and child's surname on the birth certificate pursuant to a competent court's paternity finding and order.

headings.title: Conditions for naming father of unmarried parents' child
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Restricts entering the father's name and required information for children of unmarried parents to cases with a completed section 193.215 paternity acknowledgment, court determination, or Family Support Division administrative order. Independent review revised title to reflect the conditional "only if" restriction rather than implying unconditional entry.

headings.title: Omission of father information when unnamed
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Prohibits entering any other information about the father on the birth certificate when the father is not named.

headings.title: Married woman's consented artificial insemination under subsection 5
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs completion under subsection 5 for a birth certificate of a child born to a married woman through artificial insemination with her husband's consent.

headings.title: Attestation to personal data accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Requires either parent or another informant to attest to personal data accuracy in time for five-day certificate filing.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.085:9908 (10 subsections including subdivisions in subsections 3 and 5) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked five-day filing deadlines, U.S. vs. international conveyance rules, marital/unmarried paternity conditions and 193.215 cross-references, and subsection 9 cross-reference to subsection 5. Revised subsection 7 title to "Conditions for naming father of unmarried parents' child" to preserve the "only if" restriction; retained subsections 1–6 and 8–10.

headings.title: Institution paternity-form and notice duties for unmarried mothers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note (L. 1994 merged enactments, A.L. 1997 S.B. 361, A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49). Sets institutional duties supplemental to section 193.085(2) for births to unmarried mothers in or en route to institutions: providing the section 193.215 paternity form/affidavit, filing it when completed, and giving required oral and written notice. Independent review revised title to cover subdivision (3) oral and written notice duties alongside providing and filing forms.

headings.title: Liability immunity for fulfilling subsection 1 duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants civil and criminal liability immunity to institutions, persons in charge, and designated representatives for providing forms/information or otherwise fulfilling subsection 1 duties.

headings.title: Hospital staff training contracts and free paternity materials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive Family Support Division contracting with DHSS for hospital staff assistance and training, free FSD parental rights-and-responsibilities materials, and free DHSS paternity affidavits and instructions for hospitals.

headings.title: Division training duties when no department contract exists
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the Family Support Division to provide subsection 3 hospital assistance and training itself if no contract with DHSS is developed.

headings.title: Perjury prosecution under 575.040 for intentional misidentification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. States permissive ('may be prosecuted') perjury liability under section 575.040 for an affiant who intentionally misidentifies another person as a parent.

headings.title: Public assistance grant sanctions for noncooperation and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs the Family Support Division to suspend the cash grant or remove the adult recipient's needs for lack of cooperation by public assistance recipients, qualified by federal good-cause exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.087:9909 (6 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(3) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1994 merged enactments through A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 193.085(2), 193.215, and 575.040 cross-references, permissive ("may") perjury prosecution in (5), and federal good-cause exceptions in (6). Revised subsection 1 title to "Institution paternity-form and notice duties for unmarried mothers" to cover subdivision (3) oral/written notices; retained subsections 2–6.

headings.title: Custodian report for infant of unknown parentage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Requires anyone assuming custody of a live-born infant of unknown parentage to report five listed categories of information to the local registrar within seven days.

headings.title: Place of finding entered as place of birth
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs that the place where the child was found be entered as the place of birth.

headings.title: Registered report as birth certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides that a report registered under this section constitutes the child's birth certificate.

headings.title: Sealing and inspection if child is later identified
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires placing the report in a special file if the child is identified and a birth certificate is found or obtained, barring inspection except by court order or department regulation (broader than the official catchline's 'court order only').

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.095:9910 (4 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(5) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked seven-day custodian reporting and noted subsection 4 permits inspection by court order or department regulation (broader than the official catchline's "court order only"). Retained all 4 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Delayed birth certificate filing and evidentiary rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Permits delayed filing and registration under department regulations and evidentiary rules when a Missouri birth certificate was not filed within the section 193.085 period.

headings.title: Forms and marking for certificates delayed one year or more
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires certificates registered one year or more after birth to use state-registrar forms, be marked 'Delayed', and show the delayed registration date on their face. Independent review revised title to retain the statutory threshold "one year or more".

headings.title: Endorsing summary of supporting evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires endorsing a summary statement of supporting evidence on the delayed certificate.

headings.title: Refusal to register, reasons, and appeal notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs refusal to register if minimum documentation is not submitted or validity/adequacy is reasonably questioned and deficiencies remain uncorrected, with notice of reasons and right of appeal to a court of competent jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.105:9911 (4 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 193.085 cross-reference, evidentiary endorsement, and refusal/appeal notice requirements. Revised subsection 2 title to "Forms and marking for certificates delayed one year or more" to retain the statutory "one year or more" threshold; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Court petition after delayed certificate rejection under 193.105
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49). Permits filing a signed, sworn petition with a court of competent jurisdiction to establish a birth record when a delayed certificate is rejected under section 193.105.

headings.title: Petition form and required allegations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note. Requires using a state-registrar-prescribed or approved form and specifies five mandatory allegations.

headings.title: Accompanying registrar statement and documentary evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires attaching the state registrar's section 193.105 statement and all documentary evidence previously submitted to the registrar.

headings.title: Hearing notice and state registrar appearance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires fixing a hearing and giving the state registrar thirty days' notice, and permits the registrar or representative to appear and testify.

headings.title: Court findings and order establishing birth certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs court findings and issuance of an order on a prescribed or approved form upon evidence of Missouri birth, including birth data, evidence description, and date of court action.

headings.title: Forwarding and registering court birth orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires the court clerk to forward orders by the tenth day of the following month and directs state registrar registration constituting the certificate of birth.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.115:9912 (6 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(5) of subsection 2) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2005 S.B. 74 & 49), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 193.105 cross-references, 30-day hearing notice, conditional Missouri-birth court findings, and monthly clerk forwarding deadline. Retained all 6 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Missouri Adoptee Rights Act citation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1599), and cross-reference note (453.012 for adoption petitions filed on or after August 28, 1997). Establishes the short title for sections 193.125 and 193.128.

headings.title: Adoption decree certificates, filing, and restricted opening
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history note, and 453.012 cross-reference note. Requires court-prepared certificates of decree of adoption (except under subsection 3), clerk certification, filing with the original birth certificate, and opening only by certified court order or under section 193.128.

headings.title: Stepparent adoption exception to new birth certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Bars establishing a new birth certificate after a stepparent adoption when requested by the adoptive parent or adoptive stepparent.

headings.title: Furnishing adoption report information before final decree
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires petitioners, attorneys, social welfare agencies, or knowledgeable persons to supply adoption-report information as a prerequisite to a final decree.

headings.title: Clerk reports of amended or annulled adoption decrees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires the court clerk to prepare an identifying report whenever an adoption decree is amended or annulled.

headings.title: Monthly forwarding of adoption reports to registrar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires court clerks to forward prior-month adoption, annulment, and amendment reports to the state registrar by the fifteenth day of each month or more frequently as directed.

headings.title: Forwarding reports for adoptees born outside Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Directs the state registrar to forward adoption, annulment, or amendment reports for out-of-state births to the state registrar in the state of birth.

headings.title: Birth certificates for foreign-born persons adopted in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Covers state-registrar birth certificates for Missouri adoptions of persons not born in a U.S. state, territory, possession, or interchange-agreement country, court-order-only opening of filed decrees, and evidentiary weight under section 193.235. Independent review confirmed title accuracy and noted archived source wording "not born in any state, territory or possession of the United States or country not covered by interchange agreements" retained without silent repair.

headings.title: Birth certificates for foreign-country adoptions by residents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and notes. Covers DHSS birth certificates for Missouri residents' foreign-country adoptions, surname elections, court-only subsequent name changes, required proof (translated birth certificate and decree with notarized translator oath, plus archived source reference to U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service approval), court-order-only opening, issuance on request, and evidentiary weight under sections 193.005 to 193.325.

headings.title: Unregistered adoptees under age twelve
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and notes. Distinguished from subsection 11 by applying to adopted persons under age twelve with no birth certificate on file, requiring a belated birth certificate before establishing a new certificate on a live birth form.

headings.title: Unregistered adoptees age twelve or older
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and notes. Distinguished from subsection 10 by applying to adopted persons age twelve or older with no birth certificate filed, using a delayed birth certificate form upon department-required adoption proof and sealing the adoption decree except by court order.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.125:33137 (11 subsections), history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1599), and section 453.012 cross-reference note (adoption petitions filed on or after August 28, 1997), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked stepparent opt-out in (3), archived double-negative wording in (8) and INS reference in (9) retained without repair, section 193.128 and 193.235 cross-references, and under-12 vs. 12-or-older distinction in (10)–(11). Retained all 11 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Missouri Adoptee Rights Act citation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2016 H.B. 1599, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1713). Establishes the short title for sections 193.125 and 193.128.

headings.title: Who may obtain an original birth certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes an adopted person, their attorney, or birth parents to obtain a copy of the original birth certificate from the state registrar in accordance with this section, notwithstanding section 453.121.

headings.title: Adoptee age, birthplace, application, and identification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Sets three eligibility conditions for an adopted person to receive an original birth certificate copy: age eighteen or older, born in Missouri, and written application with identification proof.

headings.title: Fees and waiting periods for uncertified copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Expresses permissive ('may') state registrar authority to require a waiting period and fee for subsection 5 uncertified copies, equal to those imposed on nonadopted persons.

headings.title: Issuance and disclaimer for uncertified original copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs issuance of an uncertified copy of the unaltered original birth certificate after fulfilling subsections 3 and 4, bearing the mandatory genealogical-only disclaimer.

headings.title: Contact preference forms, options, forwarding, and updates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including subdivisions (1) through (3), continuation div paragraph, and history note. Covers birth parent or adoptee requests, birth parent ID proof, three contact options, court-clerk forwarding at adoption, and updates at any time.

headings.title: Withholding or redaction under no-contact preferences
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Bars releasing the original birth certificate copy if both birth parents prefer no contact, and mandates redacting one parent's identifying information (as defined in section 453.121) before release if only one prefers no contact.

headings.title: Medical history forms, options, and updates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1) through (3), continuation div paragraph, and history note. Covers birth parent requests (and automatic provision with contact preference forms), three medical-history options, and updates at any time.

headings.title: Sealing and release of preference and medical forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires placing received contact preference and medical history forms in a sealed confidential envelope released only to the adopted person requesting their own original birth certificate under this section.

headings.title: Redacted medical history access under no-contact preference
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Grants the adopted person access to a copy of the medical history form with identifying information redacted when a birth parent selects a no-contact preference.

headings.title: Access for lineal descendants of deceased adoptees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Grants lineal descendants (as defined in section 453.121), upon proof of the adoptee's death, the right to obtain the original birth certificate and accompanying forms subject to subsections 7 and 10.

headings.title: Contact preference fee cap and free medical history form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Caps the contact preference form cost at the cost of obtaining an original birth certificate and prohibits charging for a medical history form. Independent review revised title to clarify that the fee cap applies specifically to contact preference forms.

headings.title: Notification period and phased access dates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note. Records the archived phased timeline: August 28, 2016 public notification period and pre-1941 adoptee access, and January 1, 2018 start of general original birth certificate issuance.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority, chapter 536 compliance, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note. Directs application-form rulemaking, permits administrative rules, requires chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance, and states nonseverability and invalidation of post-August 28, 2016 rulemaking authority and rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.128:35045 (14 subsections including subdivisions and continuation div paragraphs in subsections 6 and 8) and history note (L. 2016 H.B. 1599, A.L. 2018 H.B. 1713), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 453.121 cross-references, genealogical disclaimer, no-contact withholding/redaction, deceased-adoptee descendant access, historical 2016/2018 access dates, and post-August 28, 2016 chapter 536 nonseverability. Revised subsection 12 title to "Contact preference fee cap and free medical history form" for clarity; retained subsections 1–11 and 13–14.

headings.title: Establishing new birth certificates for adoption or legitimation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Directs establishing a new Missouri birth certificate upon adoption decrees/reports (subject to opt-out by court, adoptive parents, or adopted person) or legitimation request and proof; notes archived source verb tense ('when he or she received').

headings.title: Contents, substitution, and sealing of original records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires showing actual place and date of birth, substituting the new certificate in files, and restricting inspection of the original certificate and adoption/legitimation evidence except by court order or department rules (broader than the catchline's 'court order only').

headings.title: Amending certificates for amended adoption decrees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires amending the birth certificate upon receipt of a report of an amended decree of adoption.

headings.title: Restoring original certificates upon adoption annulment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires restoring the original birth certificate upon an annulment report or decree and restricting inspection of the new certificate and evidence except by court order or department rules.

headings.title: Sealing or forwarding other custodians' original copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires other Missouri vital-records custodians to seal from inspection or forward original birth certificate copies as directed by the state registrar. Independent review revised "local custodians" to "other custodians" to match the statutory scope "any other custodian of vital records in this state".

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.135:9914 (5 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked adoption opt-out in (1), archived verb tense ("when he or she received"), and court-order-or-department-rules inspection scope in (2) and (4) (broader than catchline). Revised subsection 5 title to "Sealing or forwarding other custodians' original copies" to match "any other custodian of vital records in this state"; retained subsections 1–4.

headings.title: Death certificate filing and electronic registration system use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 199). Covers five-day death certificate filing and conditional registration, plus mandatory use by all listed death-registration data providers of any electronic death registration system adopted under section 193.265(1) within six months of operational certification.

headings.title: Unknown place of death when remains are found
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs filing when place of death is unknown and remains are found in Missouri, showing the place found as place of death and date found as date of death.

headings.title: Deaths on moving conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguishes U.S. moving-conveyance deaths first removed in Missouri (removal place treated as place of death) from international waters, air space, or foreign-country conveyance deaths first removed in Missouri (actual place shown if determinable).

headings.title: Funeral director or final-disposition filing and data entry
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Requires the funeral director or final-disposition person to file the death certificate and obtain, verify, and enter personal data, designated medical certification under subsection 5, and other required data including embalmer name and license number. Independent review revised title to cover both funeral directors and any other person in charge of final disposition.

headings.title: Medical certification, delegation, immunity, and Social Security numbers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers 72-hour medical certification by listed practitioners, substitute natural-cause certifiers, written delegation of electronic data entry after signed cause-of-death statement, civil immunity absent gross negligence or willful misconduct, state registrar alternate methods, and recording the decedent's Social Security number.

headings.title: Natural deaths over thirty-six hours after treatment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers referral for investigation when natural-cause death occurs more than thirty-six hours after last treatment by listed practitioners, referral back to the attending practitioner, and a 36-hour attestation fallback if the practitioner refuses or is unavailable.

headings.title: Medical examiner or coroner certification for non-natural deaths
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Directs medical examiner or coroner cause-of-death determination and 72-hour medical certification after taking charge when circumstances suggest non-natural causes.

headings.title: Delayed cause-of-death notice and disposition hold
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Requires notice of delay to the funeral director or final-disposition person when cause of death cannot be determined within 72 hours, and bars final disposition until authorized.

headings.title: Court-ordered presumptive death certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Permits state registrar preparation of a death certificate upon court order with factual findings when a Missouri death is presumed and the body cannot be located, marked 'Presumptive' with registration date, court, and decree date.

headings.title: Licensee electronic-system notice and 2015 evaluation working group
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Covers DHSS electronic-system notice to chapters 334 and 335 licensees and retains the archived August 30, 2015 working-group creation and January 1, 2016 legislative report deadline.

headings.title: Coroner training requirements, attestation bars, and interim appointees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Directs DHSS to bar coroners or deputy coroners lacking current chapter 58 training from attesting death certificates, conditions assuming office on section 58.030 training completion, and directs county sheriffs to appoint temporary medical professionals to attest certificates.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.145:57518 (11 subsections including subdivisions in subsections 4 and 10) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 199), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 193.265(1) electronic system mandate, 72-hour/36-hour medical certification rules, civil immunity, presumptive death orders, historical 2015/2016 working-group dates, and chapter 58/58.030 coroner training bars. Revised subsection 4 title to "Funeral director or final-disposition filing and data entry" to include non-funeral-director disposition custodians; retained subsections 1–3 and 5–11.

headings.title: Delayed death certificate filing and evidentiary rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Permits delayed filing and registration under department rules and evidentiary requirements when a Missouri death was not registered within the section 193.145 period.

headings.title: Marking certificates registered one year or more after death
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires death certificates registered one year or more after death to be marked 'Delayed' and show the delayed registration date on their face. Independent review revised title to retain the statutory threshold "one year or more".

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.155:9916 (2 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section 193.145 cross-reference and evidentiary rules. Revised subsection 2 title to "Marking certificates registered one year or more after death" to preserve the statutory "one year or more" threshold; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Reportable spontaneous fetal deaths and filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 1999 S.B. 25, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1136). Requires reporting Missouri spontaneous fetal deaths of twenty or more completed weeks gestation or 350 or more grams weight within seven days after delivery.

headings.title: Reports for deliveries in institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Assigns report preparation and filing to the person in charge of the institution or representative when a dead fetus is delivered in an institution.

headings.title: Reports for deliveries outside institutions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Assigns report preparation and filing to the attending physician when a dead fetus is delivered outside an institution.

headings.title: Medical examiner or coroner investigations and reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires medical examiner or coroner investigation and seven-day report filing when a reportable spontaneous fetal death occurs without medical attendance or requires inquiry.

headings.title: Moving-conveyance removals and unknown-location fetal deaths
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires Missouri reporting and designates removal or discovery location as place of spontaneous fetal death for moving-conveyance removals and found fetuses with unknown death location.

headings.title: Release of reports to directly interested individuals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Expresses permissive ('may') receipt of spontaneous fetal death reports by individuals with DHSS-defined direct and tangible interest.

headings.title: Applications for certificates of birth resulting in stillbirth
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Grants either parent, or a sibling if both parents are deceased, the right to apply for a certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth based on the filed report, regardless of whether the death occurred before or after August 28, 2004.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.165:9917 (7 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2004 H.B. 1136), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 20-week/350-gram thresholds, institutional vs. non-institutional vs. coroner/ME filing roles, permissive ("may") release in (6), and parent/sibling stillbirth-certificate application rights regardless of August 28, 2004 date in (7). Retained all 7 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing and registering marriage reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2001 H.B. 157). Requires filing a report for each Missouri marriage with the department and conditions registration on completion and filing under this section.

headings.title: Preparation of marriage reports by issuing officials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the marriage-license-issuing official to prepare the report on the state-registrar form from information obtained from one party.

headings.title: Officiant certification, license return, and party certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the officiant to certify the marriage and return the witness-signed license within fifteen days after the ceremony, and requires giving a marriage certificate to the parties.

headings.title: Monthly forwarding of marriage reports to department
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires issuing officials to complete and forward prior-month returned marriage reports to the department on or before the fifteenth day of each month.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.185:9919 (4 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2001 H.B. 157), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked conditional registration in (1), 15-day officiant return and witness/party certificate duties in (3), and monthly forwarding deadline in (4). Retained all 4 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Preparing, filing, and registering dissolution or annulment records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 1996 S.B. 869), and effective-date note (Effective 7-1-97). Covers clerk filing and registration of court-granted dissolution and annulment records prepared by the petitioner or legal representative on state-registrar forms and presented with the petition.

headings.title: Monthly forwarding of dissolution and annulment records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires the court clerk to complete and forward records of prior-month dissolution and annulment decrees to the department on or before the fifteenth day of each month.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.205:9921 (2 subsections), history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 1996 S.B. 869), and effective-date note (Effective 7-1-97), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked petitioner preparation duties and clerk monthly forwarding deadline. Retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Authority and rules for amending vital records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision). Limits amendment of registered certificates or reports to procedures under sections 193.005 to 193.325 and department regulations.

headings.title: Marking amended records, date, and evidence summary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires marking amended certificates or reports 'Amended' except as otherwise provided, and endorsing the amendment date and supporting-evidence summary.

headings.title: Court-ordered name-change amendments and identifying order facts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs birth certificate amendment upon certified court name-change order and request, and requires the order to include facts identifying the birth certificate; distinguishes this second-sentence requirement from the overlapping text in subsection 8. Independent review revised title to make birth-certificate amendment explicit and clearly distinguish the second-sentence identifying-facts requirement from overlapping subsection 8.

headings.title: Refusal to amend, reasons, and appeal notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs refusal to amend when minimum documentation is missing or validity/adequacy is reasonably questioned and uncorrected, with notice of reasons and right of court appeal.

headings.title: Notifying other custodians of amended records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the state registrar to report amendments to other vital-record custodians for corresponding amendment.

headings.title: Paternity acknowledgment amendments, notices, and rescissions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and continuation sentences in subdivision (3), plus history note. Covers out-of-wedlock paternity acknowledgment amendments, 42 U.S.C. 652(a)(7) form and surname election, notarization or two disinterested witnesses, oral/written notices, section 210.823 rescission filing and FSD forwarding, and court/FSD-order requirement for changes.

headings.title: Department voluntary paternity establishment services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires the department to offer voluntary paternity establishment services.

headings.title: Birth certificate amendment for court-ordered name change
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Directs birth certificate amendment upon certified court name-change order and request; retains explicit source overlap with subsection 3's first sentence without subsection 3's second sentence requiring identifying order details.

headings.title: Court-ordered surgical sex and name change amendments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs birth certificate amendment upon receipt of a certified court order indicating surgical sex change and name change for a Missouri-born individual. Independent review revised title to preserve the statutory surgical-procedure condition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.215:9922 (9 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(3) and continuation sentences in subsection 6) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1299 Revision), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Audited the explicit overlap between subsections 3 and 8 (both directing birth-certificate amendment on certified court name-change order and request, with subsection 3 uniquely requiring identifying facts in the court order), section 210.823/42 U.S.C. 652(a)(7) paternity rules in (6), and the surgical-procedure requirement in (9). Revised subsection 3 to "Court-ordered name-change amendments and identifying order facts" and subsection 9 to "Court-ordered surgical sex and name change amendments"; retained subsections 1–2, 4–8.

headings.title: Issuance, markings, and forms for certified copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1136). Covers certified-copy issuance to applicants with direct and tangible interest, registration date, 'Delayed'/'Amended' markings and effective dates, delayed-certificate evidence endorsement, and state-registrar-approved forms and procedures.

headings.title: Evidentiary value of certified, delayed, and amended copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Makes subsection 1 certified copies equivalent to originals and prima facie evidence, qualified by leaving the evidentiary value of delayed (over one year) or amended records to the receiving judicial or administrative body or official.

headings.title: Copies and data for federal vital statistics agency
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Permits furnishing copies or data to the federal national vital statistics agency conditioned on cost sharing and statistical-only use unless authorized by the state registrar.

headings.title: Agency requests for statistical or administrative data
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Permits furnishing non-subsection-1 vital statistics copies or data to federal, state, local, public, or private agencies under regulation for statistical or administrative purposes, subject to use limits.

headings.title: Interstate agreements for transmitting vital records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Permits interstate transmission agreements for records of nonresidents or out-of-state births limited to statistical/administrative use with retention/disposition terms, and governs incoming out-of-state copies.

headings.title: Prohibition on unauthorized preparation or issuance of copies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Prohibits preparing or issuing purported originals, certified copies, or copies of vital records except as authorized by law or regulation.

headings.title: Issuance, statement, limits, and fees for stillbirth certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7, history note, and Revisor footnote ('*Word "is" appears in original rolls.' attached to 'are*'). Covers issuance under section 193.165(7) to parents or siblings if both parents are deceased, mandatory 12-point non-live-birth statement, recipient restriction, and minimal actual-cost fee authority.

headings.title: Applications for stillbirths prior to August 28, 2004
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Permits parents, or siblings if both parents are deceased, to apply for a certificate of birth resulting in stillbirth for stillbirths prior to August 28, 2004.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.255:9926 (8 subsections), history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2004 H.B. 1136), and Revisor footnote (*Word "is" appears in original rolls. on "are*" in subsection 7), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked evidentiary qualifications for delayed/amended records in (2), cost-sharing/statistical limits in (3)–(5), stillbirth 12-point disclaimer and fee authority in (7), and pre-August 28, 2004 applications in (8). Retained all 8 drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: State vital record fees, fund distribution, and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 199). Covers state certification fees ($14/$11 death; $15 birth/marriage/divorce/fetal death), juvenile-jurisdiction (211.031) fee exemptions, revenue allocation (general revenue, children's trust, endowed care cemetery audit with 33.080 non-transfer rule, coroners' fund under 58.208, public health services fund under 192.900 for automation/electronic systems), no-record search and processing fees, and free copies for relief-recipient government claims.

headings.title: Local registrar death record fees and distribution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets local registrar death-certification fees ($14 first, $11 additional), allocates $1 to state revenue for the section 58.208 Missouri coroners' fund, and deposits the remainder to the city or county health agency.

headings.title: Local non-death record fees and charter-county homelessness donations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Sets the $15 fee for birth, marriage, divorce, or fetal death certifications deposited to city or county health agencies, plus the optional $1 check-off homelessness donation for marriage licenses and birth certificates in qualifying charter counties (600,000–700,000 inhabitants).

headings.title: Local death copy precondition and county fee use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Conditions local registrar issuance of certified death copies on state registrar acceptance and registration, and requires county health agencies to retain fees for local public health purposes.

headings.title: One-time birth record fee waiver for homeless or unaccompanied youth
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Waives birth-certification fees for parents/guardians of homeless children/youth (167.020(1)) or unaccompanied youth (42 U.S.C. 11434a(6)), allows unaccompanied youth self-requests without parental consent/signature, and limits free issuance to one certificate. Independent review revised title to reflect that the waiver applies to birth certifications and is limited to one free certificate.

headings.title: One-time birth record fee waiver for domestic violence or abuse victims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Waives birth-certification fees for domestic violence or abuse victims (section 455.010) submitting specified penalty-of-perjury documentation from listed providers, attorneys, or professionals, limited to one waiver per victim. Independent review revised title to cover both domestic violence and abuse victims as defined in section 455.010.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.265:57519 (6 subsections including subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 6) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574 through A.L. 2025 H.B. 199), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked juvenile-court (211.031) and relief-claim exemptions, multi-fund allocations (including 33.080 non-transfer, 58.208, and 192.900), charter-county optional homelessness donation in (3), and one-time birth-certificate waivers in (5) and (6). Revised subsection 5 to "One-time birth record fee waiver for homeless or unaccompanied youth" and subsection 6 to "One-time birth record fee waiver for domestic violence or abuse victims"; retained subsections 1–4.

headings.title: Institution admission records for vital statistics
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574). Requires persons in charge of institutions to keep admission/confinement vital-record data from admitted persons, relatives, or knowledgeable informants, including informant name and address.

headings.title: Institution records for dead bodies and fetuses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires institutional records of release, removal, or institutional final disposition of dead bodies or dead fetuses.

headings.title: Funeral director, embalmer, sexton, and other disposition records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires funeral directors, embalmers, sextons, and others removing, transporting, or disposing of dead bodies or fetuses to maintain department-regulated receipt, transport, burial, or cremation records. Independent review revised title to reflect coverage of any other person removing, transporting, or disposing of a dead body or fetus.

headings.title: Five-year record retention and registrar inspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires retaining section 193.275 records for at least five years and making them available to the state registrar or designee upon demand.

headings.title: Furnishing vital event information upon registrar demand
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires any person with knowledge of the facts to furnish information on births, deaths, spontaneous fetal deaths, marriages, or dissolutions upon state registrar demand.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.275:9928 (5 subsections) and history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked institutional admission and body/fetus release records, five-year retention/inspection, and registrar demand authority. Revised subsection 3 title to "Funeral director, embalmer, sexton, and other disposition records" to capture "or other person"; retained subsections 1–2 and 4–5.

headings.title: False statements or information as class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17). Makes knowingly making false statements or supplying false information for vital records, applications, or amendments a class E felony.

headings.title: Counterfeiting, altering, or mutilating records with deceptive intent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Makes unauthorized making, counterfeiting, altering, amending, or mutilating vital records or certified copies with intent to deceive a class E felony.

headings.title: Deceptive use, possession, or transfer of false or another's records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes knowingly obtaining, possessing, using, selling, furnishing, or attempting such acts for deception with falsified, altered, or another person's birth records a class E felony. Independent review revised title to cover deceptive use of records relating to the birth of another living or deceased person in addition to falsified or altered records.

headings.title: Employee deceptive furnishing or processing of birth certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Makes a department or vital-statistics employee's knowing furnishing or processing of a birth certificate or certified copy with knowledge or intent of deceptive use a class E felony.

headings.title: Unauthorized possession of stolen or unlawfully obtained records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Makes unauthorized possession of a vital record, copy, or certified copy known to be stolen or unlawfully obtained a class E felony.

headings.title: Refusal to provide required information as misdemeanor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Makes knowingly refusing to provide information required by chapter 193 or its regulations a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Other knowing chapter violations or neglected duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Makes knowingly neglecting or violating chapter 193 provisions or refusing to perform chapter duties a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 193.315:9932 (7 subsections), history note (L. 1984 S.B. 574, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491), and effective-date note (Effective 1-01-17), and verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked mens rea ("knowingly", "intent to deceive") and felony/misdemeanor distinctions across all seven offenses. Revised subsection 3 title to "Deceptive use, possession, or transfer of false or another's records" to include genuine records relating to another person's birth; retained subsections 1–2 and 4–7.
